 Early voting underway in upstate New York
 BY 
 Madyson Diaz 
 Albany 
 PUBLISHED 6:00 AM ET Oct. 25, 2026 
 PUBLISHED October 25, 2026 @6:00 AM 
 SHARE 
 Early voting poll sites opened Saturday morning across New York state.
 Some voters in Albany County spoke about what voting early means to them.
 “I'm voting early because I want to make sure my vote gets counted,” Chuck Hougton said. “And I think this is a really important election.”
 “We do our due justice by our community members in making sure that we vote,” Marianna Achlaoug said.
 “You can come down here today,” Dennis Benedict said. “It's a beautiful day. It's not too bad. And, wherever you can vote, vote!”
 Last year, the New York State Board of Elections reported that close to 1.2 million New Yorkers voted early in the general election. But prior to 2019, early voting wasn’t even an option.
 “It was designed and implemented as a way to give the everyday New Yorker the opportunity to vote at a time and a place that makes sense for them,” League of Women Voters Executive Director Erica Smitka said.
 And Alison McLean Lane, the Democratic commissioner of the Albany County Board of Elections, wants everyone to take advantage of the opportunity.
 “We do have races where they have been separated by three votes,” McLean Lane said. “I have been involved in multiple manual recounts. Your vote does count.”
 And to mark the start of early voting, Republican and Democratic leaders held rallies across the state. Officals hope to inspire voters to go to the polls.
 “Just firing up people, getting them motivated to turn out to vote starting today, encouraging everyone to exercise their right to vote,” Gov. Kathy Hochul said.
 “It's very important, I think, you know, for people to get out, get that vote in early,” Senate Minority Leader Rob Ortt said. “Don't wait until election day because you never know what might happen.”
 Early voting continues through Nov. 1 and Election Day is Nov. 3.
